plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A hardy perennial prized for dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. Late-season varieties continue flowering after many other garden plants have faded, often tolerating light frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (September to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; especially popular in East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: In Japan the chrysanthemum is the emblem of the Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named after it. Its cultivation there goes back over a thousand years.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, fast-growing tree with fern-like leaves that erupts into masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. When the blossoms drop, they carpet streets and gardens in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. In Australia, a folk belief says that if a jacaranda blooms on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn and early winter with delicate, often lightly fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It is more sun-tolerant than its relative Camellia japonica and is a vital nectar source for late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub native to Mexico whose showy 'flowers' are actually colored bracts surrounding small yellow true flowers. Triggered by long nights, it reaches peak color as the holiday season approaches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown as a landscape shrub in frost-free areas and as a potted plant worldwide
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it 'cuetlaxochitl' and used its sap to make a reddish dye and to treat fevers. It is the best-selling potted flowering plant in the United States.
